title: SPIKE: Typographical/detail treatment for focus mode
description: Focus mode (dangerous-writing-app-c46.1) hides surrounding page chrome but leaves open how the remaining stage elements should look and behave once isolated: editor font size/line-height in the now-uncluttered layout, whether phase/word-count/status text stay at current size or shrink/mute further, spacing and vertical centering of the stage within the viewport, whether the grace bar treatment changes, transition/animation timing for the chrome hide/show, and any responsive (mobile) adjustments. Investigate and propose concrete typographic/layout values; not itself an implementation task.
design:
Primary constraint (per user, 2026-08-17): editor font size should render like 12-14pt print paper viewed at typical screen distance (30-50cm) — i.e. print-reading distance and screen-viewing distance are treated as roughly equal here, so matching the PHYSICAL em-square size (mm) of the print point size is what preserves equal visual angle, not the CSS spec's 'reference pixel' (which assumes a 71cm/arm's-length screen distance and would call for smaller text).

Math: standard web convention 1pt = 4/3 CSS px (96 px/in ÷ 72 pt/in), which is what browsers/OSes have used for decades and approximates physical mm reasonably well on typical consumer laptop/monitor PPI:
  12pt -> 16.00px -> 1.000rem  (4.23mm em-square)
  13pt -> 17.33px -> 1.083rem  (4.58mm em-square)
  14pt -> 18.67px -> 1.167rem  (4.94mm em-square)
(rem assumes root/html font-size is the browser default 16px — confirmed no html{font-size} override exists in style.css.)

Finding: #editor already sits at font-size: 1.18rem (=18.88px, ~14.16pt-equivalent) with line-height: 1.75 — i.e. it already lands at the TOP of the requested 12-14pt band, and 1.75 is already a generous/large screen line-height (print body leading is typically 1.2-1.45; screen reading guidance favors 1.4-1.8). So the existing value satisfies the stated constraint essentially as-is; no urgent change needed on the editor itself.

Remaining open questions for the rest of the spike's original scope (phase/timer/word-count/status sizing, vertical centering, transition timing, mobile) are unaffected by this and still open.
acceptance_criteria: A short writeup (issue notes or follow-up issues) proposes concrete font-size/line-height/spacing values for the focus-mode stage layout, covering desktop and mobile, with rationale.
notes: User direction 2026-08-17: primary focus of this spike is the print-pt-equivalent font size / large line-height for the editor, not the full original typographical checklist. Recommend either (a) close as validated (current 1.18rem/1.75 already meets the target, just document the rationale in CSS as a comment), or (b) round to the clean 14pt-equivalent value (1.1667rem / 18.67px) for a precise, documented number — difference from current is imperceptible (~0.2px). Follow-up implementation issue only needed if (b) or if mobile/other stage-element sizing also needs the same treatment.
close_reason: Resolved: #editor font-size changed from 1.18rem to the exact 14pt-equivalent 1.1667rem (18.67px, via the 96/72 px-per-pt convention), matching 12-14pt print body text at a 30-50cm screen-viewing distance. line-height (1.75) already sits in the generous/large range this calls for, left unchanged. Rest of the original spike scope (phase/timer/word-count/status sizing, vertical centering, transition timing, mobile) deferred — user narrowed focus to the print-pt font-size question only.

title: Promote "Keep going" to the primary action when a piece is in progress
description: When there is writing to carry forward, #startBtn still shows Begin/Begin again as the dominant control in #beginBox while Keep going sits demoted in .controls .actions. Worse, start() does editor.value = opts.continueText || SEED_TEXT (client.js:637), so clicking "Begin again" after a survived run REPLACES the writing on screen with the lorem ipsum seed. The text is saved first via saveAndAnnounce so it is recoverable, but the label promises continuity and delivers a wipe. Move #continueBtn into #beginBox (prominence there comes from being a top-level box in page flow, not from styling) and relabel the seed path.
design:
Four states, keyed off the same condition syncContinueBtn() reads (text.trim() && text !== SEED_TEXT), NOT 'did a run finish':
  1. nothing ever written        -> primary: Begin           / no secondary
  2. text survived or restored   -> primary: Keep going      / secondary: Start a new piece
  3. run finished, page decayed empty -> primary: Begin again / no secondary
  4. running or counting         -> primary: Stop            / no secondary

Consolidate into one syncPrimaryAction() beside syncContinueBtn(), called from start(), stop(), the finish path, and restoreTextToEditor(). startBtn.textContent is currently assigned at four scattered sites (HTML default + client.js:647, :713, :837); adding a primary/secondary dimension across all four is how state leaks.

TRAP: start() sets textContent = 'Stop' at :647 and hides continue at :642 but would not clear any .secondary class added in the DONE state -> de-emphasised Stop mid-run. Clear it alongside the textContent assignment.

CSS: .begin-box is deliberately top-level so the mobile zoom layout treats it as a first-class box (main[data-active="begin"] .begin-box / .start at style.css:770,777). It has only ever held one button; adding a second likely needs an explicit flex/gap rule in the <=619px media query.
acceptance_criteria: 1) With surviving text on the page, Keep going is the visually dominant control and Begin no longer occupies the primary slot. 2) The seed-starting button reads 'Start a new piece', not 'Begin again', whenever it would overwrite existing text. 3) Stop renders at full primary weight mid-run (no stale secondary class). 4) Decayed-empty finish still shows a single primary Begin again. 5) Mobile begin-box lays out both buttons without overflow at <=619px.
notes:
IMPLEMENTED on branch voice-and-width-fixes, commit 854ee99. Not deployed (no vt push).

WHAT CHANGED
- index.html: #continueBtn moved from .actions into #beginBox, first in DOM order.
- client.js: syncContinueBtn() -> syncPrimaryAction(active = running || counting).
  Sole owner of startBtn.textContent + continueBtn.hidden + the .secondary class.
  Called from start() as syncPrimaryAction(true), stop(), finish(),
  restoreTextToEditor(), and once at init.
- style.css: .begin-box is now flex/gap; .start.secondary is the outline
  treatment; .begin-box .continue gets .start's 2.1rem padding so the primary
  is not narrower than the secondary; mobile LAND box is flex-direction:column
  and both buttons share the 22rem/1.6rem sizing.

TWO THINGS RESOLVED DIFFERENTLY THAN THE DESIGN ASSUMED
1. No startedOnce flag. Task.stage already encodes it (LAND vs anything else),
   and adding a flag would have been a second source of truth for one fact.
2. Side effect worth knowing: a countdown cancelled before the clock starts
   sets setStage("LAND"), so the button now reads "Begin" there rather than
   "Begin again". More accurate — nothing happened — but it is a visible
   change beyond the stated scope.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
1. Keep going dominant when text survives  — VERIFIED (state table simulated)
2. Seed button reads 'Start a new piece'   — VERIFIED, incl. partial decay
   (a few surviving words still routes to state 2, correctly: there IS text
   to overwrite)
3. Stop at full weight mid-run             — VERIFIED (Stop entered directly
   from the DONE state clears .secondary)
4. Decayed-empty shows single Begin again  — VERIFIED
5. Mobile <=619px lays out both buttons    — NOT VERIFIED. Reasoned only:
   .begin-box is flex-direction:column so the width:100% .start cannot
   collide with .continue. No browser check (user preference: no
   claude-in-chrome in this project). Needs a human eye at <=619px.
close_reason: Implemented in 854ee99 on voice-and-width-fixes. Criteria 1-4 verified by simulating syncPrimaryAction across all four states plus the partial-decay and cancelled-countdown edges. Criterion 5 (mobile <=619px layout) is reasoned, not tested — needs a human eye after deploy. Restoring an entry whose text is exactly SEED_TEXT now hides Keep going where the old unconditional unhide showed it; that is the finish path's existing behaviour, so restore is now consistent rather than special-cased. The reason such an entry can exist at all is filed as dangerous-writing-app-8a6.

title: Phase 3: version deltas so rows read differently
description:
Continuations are supersets, so near-identical versions look identical. Show what changed since the prior version:
- Latest version: full snippet.
- Older versions: appended tail (delta since prior) + word delta (+N words).
Makes 'which version to pick' answerable at a glance.

title: Phase 4: retrospective management (move/split/merge/delete)
description:
Fix heuristic false positives (e.g. kept piece A's text at the top but pivoted to writing B).
- Rename piece; move a version to another piece; split a version off into its own piece; merge two versions/pieces; delete.
- Backend: POST /api/pieces/:id/rename, /api/versions/:id/move, /api/versions/:id/split.

title: Phase 2: classification affordances + titles/rename
description:
Let the user control new-vs-version, not just the heuristic.
- Start: make Keep-going (continuation) vs Begin again (new piece) explicit + overridable via a small split control.
- Finish/save: non-blocking tag 'new version of <title>' or 'new piece' with inline title + reclassify.
- Every piece gets a title (auto from first line/first words), editable.
- Rename a piece in the entries view.

title: Phase 1: piece-boundary detection, migration, horizontal-rule grouping
description:
Group-bound, shippable alone. Build writing with a piece identity so distinct pieces can be told apart from versions.

- Schema: pieces_2 + writing_versions_2 replacing writing_sessions (new tables per AGENTS; no in-place ALTER).
- Migration: fold existing writing_sessions rows into pieces/versions via the heuristic (prefix continuation + time gap -> new piece).
- /api/sessions returns grouped {pieces:[{id,title,versions:[{id,text,savedAt}]}]}; /api/save accepts optional pieceId hint (null=auto).
- Entries view groups versions under a piece; horizontal .piece-rule between distinct pieces (the 'state change' mark). Keep existing restore-on-click.

Acceptance: 1) existing history migrates + groups correctly. 2) horizontal rules between pieces. 3) versions group under their piece. 4) save still folds continuations into the same piece.
notes:
IMPLEMENTED on branch writing-management (commit 51758d0), NOT deployed.

Departure from decision 3, deliberate: foldsIntoPiece() is bidirectional (a.startsWith(b) || b.startsWith(a)), not one-way. Decay means a run can end SHORTER than the version it carried forward (save 400 words, keep going, drift to 350), and the one-way rule calls that a new piece — fragmenting a piece for exactly the writer having a bad session. Revert = drop one term in piece-heuristic.ts.

Acceptance status:
  1) history migrates + groups correctly — DEPLOY-GATED, not verifiable locally (sqlite is remote)
  2) horizontal rules between pieces — implemented (.piece-rule), box model reviewed, not browser-verified
  3) versions group under their piece — DEPLOY-GATED
  4) save folds continuations into the same piece — logic implemented; predicate covered by 8 passing unit tests

Verified locally: deno check --allow-import main.ts clean; 8/8 tests in piece-heuristic.test.ts. NOTE: repo is not deno-fmt clean and was not before this change, so fmt was deliberately not run.

All three consumers of the old shapes were checked: /api/save response consumer reads only data.saved (unchanged); /api/sessions consumer updated to data.pieces; getDebugServerState now reports pieceCount + versionCount separately instead of sessionCount.

DEPLOY IS THE RISK: first cold start after vt push runs migrateLegacySessions() against real writing history. Not pushed — awaiting explicit go-ahead.

title: Writing / version management: distinguish pieces from versions
description:
Redesign how finished writing is stored and shown so a user can tell a NEW PIECE apart from a VERSION of an earlier piece, and can choose which one to open. Pain: the flat 'Previous entries' list mixes continuations and distinct pieces into identical rows ('Oct 31 4:02pm · 412 words' + snippet), so you can't tell which to pick.

MODEL
- Piece: a coherent writing artifact (title, created, updated), owned by one user.
- Version: one saved run/snapshot; always belongs to exactly one Piece (a Piece has >=1 Versions).
- Classification question becomes: does this run create a NEW Piece, or is it a new Version of an existing Piece?

CLASSIFICATION — how the app determines it (a)
Three signals in order; explicit user marker wins, else prefix-continuation against the latest Version of the same Piece, else time-gap (large gap -> new piece even on prefix match), else default to NEW PIECE (conservative).
Runs at start-of-run and at finish/save; client sends a continue/new hint rather than letting the server guess alone.

USER CONTROL (b)
- Start: make Keep-going (continuation) vs Begin again (new piece) explicit/overridable.
- Finish/save: non-blocking tag 'new version of <title>' or 'new piece' with inline title + reclassify.
- Retrospective (entries view): rename Piece, move/split/merge/delete Versions to fix heuristic false positives.

SERVER / SCHEMA (Val Town sqlite; new tables per AGENTS)
- pieces_2(id,user_id,title,created_at,updated_at)
- writing_versions_2(id,piece_id,text,saved_at) replacing writing_sessions
- migrate existing writing_sessions via same heuristic; /api/sessions returns grouped {pieces:[{title,versions}]}; add rename/move/split endpoints; save accepts optional pieceId hint.
- current LIMIT 5 must become grouping-aware or paginated.

UI
- Entries view groups by Piece with a horizontal RULE between distinct pieces (the 'state change' mark). Within a piece, versions show DELTA since prior version (+N words, appended tail) instead of full text — makes near-identical continuations distinct. Every Piece gets a title (auto from first line, editable).

ROADMAP
Phase 1 (foundation, shippable alone): piece-boundary detection + migration + horizontal-rule grouping.
Phase 2: explicit classification affordances (finish-time tag, keep-going/new-piece control) + titles/rename.
Phase 3: version deltas so rows read differently.
Phase 4: retrospective management (move/split/merge/delete).

DECISIONS STILL OPEN (see notes): anonymous/local-only scope; title source; time-gap threshold.
design:
# Design notes

## Current state
- localStorage `dangerous-writing:last` = single last-draft object {text, savedAt} (all users).
- SQLite `writing_sessions(id,user_id,username,text,saved_at)`, keyed by val.town user id, only when signed in.
- /api/save: folds a new save into the latest row if text.startsWith(last.text) (continuation); else INSERT.
- /api/sessions: returns last 5 rows DESC.
- Previous entries panel: flat list, each row = time + wordcount + 90-char snippet; click restores text to editor.

## Why flat list is confusing
Continuations (Keep going) and distinct pieces (Begin again) both become near-identical rows. No grouping/title/delta.

## Horizontal-rule increment (highest value, lowest risk)
Pure display, no new affordances: server groups versions under pieces, client renders a piece header + its versions, with a .piece-rule between distinct pieces. This answers 'which to choose' with minimal code and is a valid Phase-1 deliverable on its own.

## Open decisions
1. Anonymous/local-only users: recommend piece mgmt for signed-in only; local single-draft restore unchanged (local-only piece store = later).
2. Title source: auto from first line/first words, editable. Confirm.
3. Time-gap threshold for new piece: start with a number (e.g. 24h), refine.
4. Keep-going (carries text) is naturally a continuation; Begin again is naturally fresh — make this an explicit override, confirm placement.

title: Let the writer set a theme / prompt / writing goal for the session
description:
Before (or during) a session, the writer should be able to tell the app what they're working on — a theme, a prompt, a writing goal, etc. — and have it carried through the session (shown on screen, and usable as context for the AI-takeover if that path is enabled).

Constraint: stay FLEXIBLE for now. We don't yet know the right shape of this data (free-text prompt? structured goal? reusable templates? per-session or saved?), so don't lock in a rigid model. Start with the simplest thing that works and leaves room to grow:
- free-form text is fine for now
- avoid a heavyweight schema / new storage table until usage justifies it
- reuse the existing persistence path (localStorage via the Task object) rather than a backend DB
- a note in the code (or this issue's children) where a richer model would slot in later

Open questions (do NOT block on these for v1):
- should the setting be per-session or global?
- where exactly on screen should it live / be editable?
- should it feed the AI takeover as a prompt/context? (ties into wrg's gating)
acceptance_criteria: Writer can enter a theme/prompt/goal and it persists across reload (via existing localStorage path). It displays somewhere in the session UI. No schema/DB changes introduced for v1. If it feeds the AI-takeover, that stays gated on server GREENPT_API_KEY per issue wrg.

title: AI takeover UI must gate on server GREENPT_API_KEY, not just the aiMode toggle
description:
Currently the AI-takeover UI (phase "Passing the pen", triggerAiTakeover())
fires purely off the client-side aiMode checkbox in client.js. It never
checks whether the server actually has AI configured.

getDebugServerState() in main.ts already computes this as
greenptConfigured: !!Deno.env.get("GREENPT_API_KEY"), surfaced today only
on the /debug page — it is not exposed to the main app or to client.js.

Failure scenario: aiMode is checked but GREENPT_API_KEY is unset. loop()
hits idle >= inactivityMs, sets phase "Passing the pen" and status "Start
typing to take it back.", then triggerAiTakeover()'s fetch to /ai/continue
fails into "The machine faltered. Keep writing." Meanwhile the non-AI
decay branch never runs (aiMode.checked short-circuits it), so the
writer's text is neither erased nor continued — nothing happens, and the
UI has already promised a takeover that can't occur.

Fix direction: surface greenptConfigured to the client (e.g. add it to
the existing /api/me response, since refreshAuth() already calls that on
load) and use it to disable/hide the AI takeover toggle, or fall back to
the decay path, when the server has no key configured.

title: Joyful mobile-first redesign (calm, friendly, simple)
description: Redesign the UI to be simple, friendly, and calm, tuned for mobile-first in-browser use on val.town (no PWA). Keep the focus-mode chrome-hiding behavior. Deliverable: refreshed layout/typography/color/motion/copy that feels welcoming rather than harsh, working on a phone viewport.
notes: Implemented: warm soft cream/charcoal/sage/lilac/terracotta palette; sentence-case serif voice (removed harsh all-caps mono labels + alarm-red demo button); softened microcopy in client.js (no Brutal/wrestle/vanishing/dissolving/takes over; calmer phases Breathe/Fading/Shared/Done, friendlier win/loss lines); rewrote masthead lede, kicker, editor placeholder, colophon; mobile-first touches (full-width Begin, 3rem tap targets, safe-area clearance for grace bar). Focus-mode + enlarged editor type preserved.

title: Focus mode: hide page chrome while a session is active
description: Add a focus-mode body state that hides the masthead/lede, authbar, settings controls (sliders, AI toggle, entries panel), and footer/colophon while a countdown or writing run is active, leaving the stage (editor, timer, progress bar, grace bar) and the Stop control visible. Focus mode engages the moment Begin/demo is pressed, before the countdown starts, and clears when the run finishes or is stopped.
acceptance_criteria: Clicking Begin (or Start demo) hides masthead, authbar, settings controls, and footer immediately, before the 3-2-1 countdown runs. The editor, timer, progress bar, grace bar, and Stop button stay visible and usable throughout. Chrome reappears when the run ends (finish) or is stopped early (stop).
close_reason: Implemented: body.focus-mode hides masthead, authbar, settings controls, and colophon while a countdown/run is active, keeping the stage and Stop button visible. Toggled on in start() before runCountdown(), off in stop() and finish().

title: Focus mode for when I'm writing
description: Add a distraction-free writing mode that hides the surrounding page chrome (masthead/lede, settings controls, footer/colophon) while a writing session is active, leaving just the editor, timer, progress bar, and grace bar visible. Goal: let the writer stay visually locked onto the text instead of the settings panel and marketing copy above/below it.

title: Add 'Keep going' option to resume writing after a session ends
description:
When a run finishes (finish() in client.js:557-605), the only option offered is 'Begin again', which calls start() and always reseeds the editor with SEED_TEXT (client.js:440), discarding the just-finished text from the live editor (it is still saved to storage via saveAndAnnounce, but not carried into the next session). Add a 'Keep going' action alongside 'Begin again' so a writer can continue drafting from where they left off instead of only being able to restart fresh with the lorem ipsum seed.

## Context
See client.js finish() (~L557-605) and start() (~L425-468).
design: Capture finished text when finish() runs. Add a 'Keep going' control that calls start({ continueText }) which skips SEED_TEXT seeding, loads continueText into the editor instead, and preserves caret at end. Decide whether Keep going re-runs the 3-2-1 countdown or jumps straight to beginRun().
acceptance_criteria: After a run ends, the writer can choose 'Keep going' to start a new timed run with the editor pre-loaded with their just-finished text (cursor at the end), as an alternative to 'Begin again' which reseeds with SEED_TEXT. Both options remain available and behave independently.
close_reason: Implemented: continueBtn ('Keep going') carries the on-screen text into a fresh timed run via start({continueText}). Standard 3-2-1 countdown kept so the grace clock doesn't start before the writer's hands are back on the keys. Verified with a headless linkedom harness (14/14 checks). Follow-ups filed: dangerous-writing-app-y9s (decay balance), dangerous-writing-app-hil (demoBtn).

title: Surface grace period to the writer during a run
description:
Currently the grace/idle period (inactivityMs) is never shown to the user as a live countdown. The only mention is a one-time status line in demo mode ("Demo: 30s to survive, 2s grace. Brutal." - client.js:462); normal runs never state the grace value at all. The only in-run feedback is indirect: phase text changes to "Hold on..." and a warning CSS/status kicks in only during the final min(1500ms, 60% of grace) window before decay/AI-takeover triggers (client.js:716-741, loop()). Consider surfacing the grace countdown more explicitly (e.g. a numeric or visual indicator of remaining idle budget) so writers understand how much silence they have before losing text.

## Context
See client.js loop() (idle/warning logic ~L665-745) and start()/runCountdown() for where grace value is (or isn't) communicated.
acceptance_criteria: User can tell, at a glance while writing, roughly how much idle/grace time remains before decay or AI takeover triggers - not just in the final ~1.5s warning window.
close_reason: Added a viewport-fixed grace meter (#graceBar): a draining rule plus 'N.Ns of silence left' label pinned to the bottom of the window so it stays visible however far the writing scrolls. Fades in only once 25% of the budget is spent (GRACE_REVEAL), turns red with the existing warning ramp, sits empty at zero. Runs now also open by stating the budget ('5 seconds of silence allowed — then your words start to go.'), cleared on the first keystroke. Verified headlessly (28/28 checks); pushed to Val Town.

title: Stopping a run you never typed in saves the lorem ipsum as your writing
description:
start() seeds the editor with SEED_TEXT and never clears it — the writer types over and around it. stop() in the !wasCounting branch calls saveAndAnnounce(editor.value, ...) unconditionally. So: Begin, type nothing, click Stop before the grace period elapses, and the untouched lorem ipsum is written to localStorage (dangerous-writing:last) and POSTed to /api/save as a session. It then shows up in the entries panel as a piece you wrote.

Not reachable via finish(): grace maxes at 20s and the goal floor is 30s, so decay or AI always alters the text before a run ends. The early-Stop window is the only path.

Fix is a guard in stop(): treat editor.value === SEED_TEXT as nothing-to-save, the same test syncPrimaryAction() already uses for whether there is anything to carry forward. Once pieces_2 lands (dangerous-writing-app-b0y.1) this also means seed text can open a piece on the server.
acceptance_criteria: Begin a run, type nothing, Stop before the grace period elapses: no entry is created locally or server-side, and the status does not claim anything was saved.

title: Beads DB schema skew (v65) vs binary (v53) — needs 1.2.1 recovery
description: Every bd command requires BD_IGNORE_SCHEMA_SKEW=1 because the local beads Dolt DB is at schema v65 (migrated by the accidental v1.2.1 release) while the installed binary knows up to v53. Follow the recovery guide at https://github.com/gastownhall/beads/blob/v1.2.2/docs/RECOVERY-1.2.1.md to roll the cursor back to v53. Audit-event versioning is paused until recovered.

title: Continued runs fill Previous entries with near-duplicate snapshots
description: saveAndAnnounce() writes the full editor text to localStorage and POSTs it to /api/save at the end of every run. With 'Keep going' (dangerous-writing-app-h0f), continuing one piece across five runs inserts five writing_sessions rows, each a superset of the previous. /api/sessions returns LIMIT 5, so the Previous entries panel fills up with near-identical snapshots of a single piece and older, distinct sessions fall off.
design: Options: pass a session id through start({continueText}) and UPDATE the existing row instead of inserting; or de-duplicate server-side when the new text starts with an existing row's text; or raise the LIMIT and group continuations in the UI.
acceptance_criteria: Continuing a piece across several runs leaves the Previous entries panel showing distinct pieces, not a stack of supersets.

title: finish() never re-enables the Start demo button
description: In client.js finish() re-enables minutes, seconds and aiMode but not demoBtn, which start() disabled. stop() does re-enable it. So after a run ends normally, 'Start demo' stays greyed out until the page is reloaded or a run is stopped early. Pre-existing, noticed while implementing dangerous-writing-app-h0f.
acceptance_criteria: After a run finishes normally, the Start demo button is clickable again.

title: Carried-over text makes the decay fail state hard to reach
description: 'Keep going' (dangerous-writing-app-h0f) starts a run pre-loaded with the writer's existing text. Non-AI decay erases from the end at DECAY_CHARS_PER_SEC=12 (client.js loop()) and finish(false) only fires when editor.value.length === 0, so a 2000-character carry-over needs ~167s of continuous idling to lose — usually longer than the whole run. The longer you write, the safer idling becomes, which inverts the premise.
design: Options: scale decay rate with text length; add a per-idle-period character floor; or decay a fixed fraction of the text. Note the carried text is already persisted by saveAndAnnounce at finish(), so this is game balance, not data loss.
acceptance_criteria: Idling past the grace period during a continued run carries a comparable stake to idling during a fresh run.
